Emerging Fungal Pathogens & Disease Dynamics

1. A One Health Approach to Understanding Biology of Emerging Fungal Zoonoses to Mitigate in high-density farming Examine dynamics of animal agriculture and global trade in compounding cross-species pathogenic fungal infection and develop integrated surveillance solutions. 2. Understanding the impact of climate change on fungal biodiversity and emergence of fungal pathogens. Investigate how environmental changes and human migration influence the distribution, adaptation, and evolution of pathogenic fungi. 3. Examining viral pandemics and the co-morbidity to increase susceptibility to co-infection of opportunistic fungal infections. Using the co-infection as examples (COVID-19 and mucormycosis) to develop treatment protocols and risk prediction.

Antifungal Drug Resistance & Novel Therapeutics

4. Antifungal Resistance Mechanisms and Monitoring in clinical and agricultural contexts. Evaluate azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus and Trichophyton indotineae existence in agricultural nematodes, and its connection with fungicide, azole use in agriculture. 5. AI-led repurposing and discovery of antifungals from natural and synthetic product libraries. Use machine-learning and bioinformatics to find compounds ignored that work against resistant strains of fungi. 6. Next-generation antifungal development with novel mechanisms. From Olorofim to GPI inhibitors. Ultimately, facilitate the clinical development of classes of new compounds, while navigating and overcoming challenges to bioavailability and toxicity in host.

Diagnostics and Pathogen Detection

7. Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Fungal Infections via AI and Microfluidics Develop rapid, field-deployable diagnostic tools using lab-on-a-chip systems and automated microscopy 8. Integrating Molecular Phylogeny with Clinical Mycology: A Practical Diagnostic Taxonomy Respond to the fragmented nature of fungal taxonomy to better attend to clinical relevance and diagnostic clarity

Drug Discovery & Synthetic Biology

9. Mineralising Cryptic Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs) in Rare Fungi for New Bioactive Compounds Use genome mining and heterologous expression of BGCs to characterise, and discover new secondary metabolites that may have therapeutic potential 10. Synthetic Biology and Semi-Synthetic Pathways for Scalable Production of Fungal Metabolites Design affordable fermentation and modification pathways to commercialise fungal-derived drugs If any of these topics sparked an idea, that’s a great place to start!
